rf_publication_contract.zero: Reports0 when no satellite update exists or the last satellite update is older than 5000ms; a zero count is conservative evidence that the cached position must no longer authorize launch.
rf_publication_contract.gps_data: Three float coordinates published only on successful NMEA receive with gps_has_fix. Packet timestamp is publication time; no separate acquisition epoch or boot-session token exists in this message.

policy: A current RF zero-satellite publication immediately clears the RF fix slot. Other boards cannot revoke RF lock. Positive satellite count alone cannot establish a lock.
UTC zero-satellite publications older than an acceptedUTC fix or newer zero watermark are ignored. GPS with publication timestamp equal to/before the loss watermark cannot revive the lock.

After explicit no-fix, boot-relative GPS alone cannot prove recovery: there is no known boot-session identity, so large delayed pre-reboot counters are not treated as new fixes. Initial receipt-age behavior before any explicit loss remains unchanged.

A later comparable UTC GPS publication restores lock. For boot-to-UTC transition, use a fixed synchronized UTC receipt bound; if UTC was absent/epoch 0 at loss, establish that bound once when comparable UTC becomes available, rather than moving it on every attempt.

GPS receipt/cache reseeding cannot erase source age or the loss fence. Existing 15s freshness and 5s future-skew policy remains; model aging uses virtual monotonic time while physical GPSD/remote position aging remains wall time.

old_ignore_zero.scope: Diagnostic mutation in an ignored isolated source clone, not a frozen production candidate.
